This vignette predicts structural divergence **per normal mode** and fits it to
data. Its sibling, the [site analysis vignette](site-analysis.html), runs the same
arc **per residue**; the two are companion views of one model. For a short
end-to-end tour of both axes, see the [package overview](msamodel.html).

A single mutation displaces the structure by a vector `dr`. The site form squares that
displacement per residue; the mode form projects `dr` onto the elastic-network normal
modes and squares each mode's contribution. The two are the same displacement written in
two different bases, so for any single mutant the totals agree — summing over residues
and summing over modes give the same number. Low-index modes are the soft, collective motions of
the protein; the mode profile shows **which motions** carry the predicted
divergence, where the site profile shows **which residues** do. We use the worked
example `1znb_A` (zinc beta-lactamase), whose data ship as the `znb_*` datasets.

Two verbs carry the whole vignette. `calculate_profiles()` returns the divergence
profile at a given `(a1, a2)` — use it for the profile itself; `calculate_decomposition()`
returns the four nested models plus their mutation/stability/activity split — use it when
you want that breakdown. Each returns a list with a `$site` tibble (per residue) and a
`$mode` tibble (per normal mode); this per-mode vignette reads `$mode` throughout.

## 1. Setup

Everything starts from your two inputs: a structure file and a vector of
active-site residue numbers. We use the worked example `1znb_A` (zinc
beta-lactamase) that ships with the package; swap in your own at the two marked
lines.


```r
library(msamodel)
library(dplyr)      # data-wrangling verbs (mutate, left_join, ...) used below
library(tidyr)      # pivot_longer, to reshape profiles for plotting
library(purrr)      # map_dfr, for the parameter sweeps
library(readr)      # read_csv, for the example data files
library(ggplot2)    # the figures; optional — skip it if you only want the tables
```

Both inputs are files; point these at your own to run the vignette on your protein.
The active-site table is one residue per row, keyed by `pdb` and `chain`, so a single
file can serve many proteins — filter out the chain you are modelling.


```r
pdb_file    <- system.file("extdata", "1znb_A.pdb", package = "msamodel")          # <- your PDB
active_file <- system.file("extdata", "znb_active_site.csv", package = "msamodel") # <- your active sites

pdb_site_active <- read_csv(active_file, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(pdb == "1znb", chain == "A") |>
  pull(pdb_site)

pdb_site_active
#> [1]  99 101 103 162 181 184 193 223
```

`msamodel` reads the structure, builds an elastic network model (`wt`), and runs a
single-point-mutation scan (`spm`). The arguments below are the model's defaults — keep
them for a first run (the [site analysis](site-analysis.html) vignette explains what
each controls). The scan takes a minute or two — it is the one slow step here.


```r
wt_pdb <- bio3d::read.pdb(pdb_file)
wt     <- setup_enm(wt_pdb, node = "ca", model = "ming_wall", d_max = 10.5, frustrated = FALSE)
spm    <- generate_spm_data(wt, n_mutations = 10, model = "lfenm", sigma = 0.3,
                            min_sd = 2, pdb_site_active = pdb_site_active, seed = 1024)
```

The per-mode divergence the verbs below read lives in `spm$dr2_njm`, a matrix with
one row per mutant and one column per normal mode:


```r
dim(spm$dr2_njm)   # rows = mutants (228 sites x 10 mutations), columns = normal modes
#> [1] 2280  678
```

> **For your own protein you can run the mode prediction (sections 1–4). The mode
> fit (section 5) needs an observed per-mode divergence profile** — a measured divergence
> for each normal mode — which is not something you typically have: measured divergence
> is per residue, not per mode. `msamodel` does not produce a per-mode observed profile,
> so the fit here runs on a **synthetic** stand-in, loaded where the fit begins
> (section 5), purely to show the fitting machinery.

## 2. Divergence profile at given (a1, a2)

The model runs at any `(a1, a2)` you choose. `calculate_profiles()` returns the
divergence profile; we take the per-mode reading with `$mode`. Its tibble has the mode
index `mode` and the profile `lrmsd_msa`. That value column is named exactly as on the
site axis — both branches share one vocabulary, and only the key column differs — so
anything you write for one axis reads the other unchanged.
The `metric` argument picks the quantity: `"lrmsd"` (used through sections 2–4) is
the absolute profile, and `"nlrmsd"` is the same profile with its mean subtracted off (its
shape), which section 5 uses to compare against data. Here we pick illustrative values
(`a1 = 2`, `a2 = 500`); section 5 estimates them from data instead.


```r
a1 <- 2; a2 <- 500
profile <- calculate_profiles(spm, a1, a2, metric = "lrmsd")$mode
head(profile)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 2
#>    mode lrmsd_msa
#>   <int>     <dbl>
#> 1     1     -2.91
#> 2     2     -2.92
#> 3     3     -2.49
#> 4     4     -2.72
#> 5     5     -2.82
#> 6     6     -3.00
```


```r
ggplot(profile, aes(mode, lrmsd_msa)) +
  geom_line(colour = "grey40") +
  geom_point(size = 0.7, colour = "grey20") +
  labs(
    title = sprintf("Mode-divergence profile (a1 = %g, a2 = %g)", a1, a2),
    subtitle = "Low mode indices are the soft, collective motions",
    x = "Normal-mode index", y = "lrmsd"
  )
```

![plot of chunk profile-plot](mode-analysis_files/figure-html/profile-plot-1.png)

The lowest-index (softest) modes carry the most divergence: a handful of
collective motions account for most of the predicted structural change.

## 3. Decomposing the profile at given (a1, a2)

The mode profile at a chosen `(a1, a2)` splits into additive mutation,
stability-selection, and activity-selection contributions, built from four **nested
model variants** — the model with one or both selection pressures switched off:

| Variant | a1 (stability) | a2 (activity) | meaning |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| **MM** | 0 | 0 | mutation only — no selection |
| **MS** | a1 | 0 | mutation + stability selection |
| **MA** | 0 | a2 | mutation + activity selection |
| **MSA** | a1 | a2 | full model — both selections |

(`MSA` — mutation, stability, activity — names the full model, and is the `msa` you see
throughout the function names.) `calculate_decomposition()` returns, in one `$mode`
tibble, both the four nested profiles (`lrmsd_mm`, `lrmsd_ms`,
`lrmsd_ma`, `lrmsd_msa`) and their split (`phi_mut`, `phi_stab`, `phi_act`):


```r
decomposition <- calculate_decomposition(spm, a1, a2, metric = "lrmsd")$mode   # a1 = 2, a2 = 500
head(decomposition)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 8
#>    mode lrmsd_mm lrmsd_ms lrmsd_ma lrmsd_msa phi_mut phi_stab phi_act
#>   <int>    <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl>    <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1     1    -1.80    -1.51    -3.48     -2.91   -1.80  0.289    -1.40 
#> 2     2    -2.14    -1.76    -3.55     -2.92   -2.14  0.380    -1.16 
#> 3     3    -2.41    -2.16    -2.96     -2.49   -2.41  0.249    -0.329
#> 4     4    -2.55    -2.56    -2.72     -2.72   -2.55 -0.00555  -0.161
#> 5     5    -2.63    -2.60    -2.85     -2.82   -2.63  0.0276   -0.226
#> 6     6    -2.68    -2.58    -3.25     -3.00   -2.68  0.0992   -0.420
```


```r
model_colours <- c(MM = "#FF8C00", MS = "#0000CD", MA = "#1B9E77", MSA = "#C41E3A")
nested_profiles_long <- decomposition |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(lrmsd_mm, lrmsd_ms, lrmsd_ma, lrmsd_msa),
                      names_to = "model", values_to = "lrmsd_msa") |>
  mutate(model = factor(toupper(sub("lrmsd_", "", model)),
                        levels = c("MM", "MS", "MA", "MSA")))
ggplot(nested_profiles_long, aes(mode, lrmsd_msa, colour = model)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = model_colours) +
  labs(title = sprintf("Nested-model mode profiles (a1 = %g, a2 = %g)", a1, a2),
       x = "Normal-mode index", y = "lrmsd", colour = "model")
```

![plot of chunk nested-profiles](mode-analysis_files/figure-html/nested-profiles-1.png)

The **sequential** decomposition adds one selection pressure at a time along
MM → MS → MSA; each $\phi$ term is the incremental divergence contributed by the
next pressure. (MA — activity alone — is the fourth variant, not a step on this path;
it shows activity selection's effect on its own. The decomposition uses MM, MS, MSA.)

$$
\phi_{\text{mut}}  = \text{lrmsd}_{\text{mm}}, \qquad
\phi_{\text{stab}} = \text{lrmsd}_{\text{ms}} - \text{lrmsd}_{\text{mm}}, \qquad
\phi_{\text{act}}  = \text{lrmsd}_{\text{msa}} - \text{lrmsd}_{\text{ms}}
$$

By construction these sum to the full prediction. The four nested profiles are in the
`decomposition` tibble above when you want to *see* them, and the three `phi_*` columns are
there when you want the split directly:


```r
# Paper component colours: mutation = orange, stability = blue, activity = red.
component_colours <- c(phi_mut = "#FF8C00", phi_stab = "#0000CD", phi_act = "#C41E3A")
decomposition_long <- decomposition |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(phi_mut, phi_stab, phi_act),
                      names_to = "component", values_to = "phi") |>
  mutate(component = factor(component, levels = names(component_colours)))
ggplot(decomposition_long, aes(mode, phi, colour = component)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey80") +
  geom_line() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = component_colours, guide = "none") +
  facet_wrap(~ component, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(title = sprintf("Decomposition of the mode profile (a1 = %g, a2 = %g)", a1, a2),
       x = "Normal-mode index", y = "contribution to lrmsd")
```

![plot of chunk decomposition-given](mode-analysis_files/figure-html/decomposition-given-1.png)

## 4. How the profile depends on a1 and a2

Stability selection (`a1`, with `a2 = 0`) and activity selection (`a2`, with `a1 = 0`)
shape the mode profile differently. We vary one parameter at a time and overlay the
resulting profiles.


```r
# Stability sweep: vary a1, hold a2 = 0
a1_values <- c(0, 1, 2, 4, 8)
sweep_a1 <- purrr::map_dfr(a1_values, function(a1)
  calculate_profiles(spm, a1, 0, metric = "lrmsd")$mode |> mutate(a1 = a1))

# Activity sweep: vary a2, hold a1 = 0
a2_values <- c(0, 31, 127, 511, 2047)
sweep_a2 <- purrr::map_dfr(a2_values, function(a2)
  calculate_profiles(spm, 0, a2, metric = "lrmsd")$mode |> mutate(a2 = a2))
```


```r
ggplot(sweep_a1, aes(mode, lrmsd_msa, colour = factor(a1), group = a1)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_colour_viridis_d(end = 0.9) +
  labs(title = "Stability sweep (a2 = 0)", x = "Normal-mode index",
       y = "lrmsd", colour = "a1")
```

![plot of chunk sweep-a1](mode-analysis_files/figure-html/sweep-a1-1.png)


```r
ggplot(sweep_a2, aes(mode, lrmsd_msa, colour = factor(a2), group = a2)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_colour_viridis_d(option = "C", end = 0.9) +
  labs(title = "Activity sweep (a1 = 0)", x = "Normal-mode index",
       y = "lrmsd", colour = "a2")
```

![plot of chunk sweep-a2](mode-analysis_files/figure-html/sweep-a2-1.png)

Increasing `a1` suppresses divergence across the soft modes (stability selection
damps the collective motions); increasing `a2` reshapes the soft-mode divergence
according to selection on activity.

## 5. Fitting a1 and a2 to observed divergence

Fitting needs an **observed** per-mode divergence profile: two vectors, the mode indices
and the observed log-RMSD at each. The real obstacle on this axis is not the format but
the data itself — measured divergence is naturally *per residue*, and turning it into a
per-mode profile is not something `msamodel` does.

So the example profile used here is **synthetic**, not empirical: it was produced by
fitting the site model to the real per-residue data, evaluating the mode forward map at
that estimate, and adding seeded Gaussian noise. It exists only to run the fitting
machinery end to end, and the `_syn` in its file name is there to keep that visible.
Numbers obtained from it say nothing about zinc beta-lactamase.


```r
observed_file <- system.file("extdata", "znb_lrmsd_obs_mode_syn.csv", package = "msamodel")
observed      <- read_csv(observed_file, show_col_types = FALSE)   # <- your observed mode profile
head(observed)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 2
#>    mode lrmsd_obs
#>   <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1     1     -2.00
#> 2     2     -2.32
#> 3     3     -2.17
#> 4     4     -2.14
#> 5     5     -2.50
#> 6     6     -2.86
```

`fit_lrmsd_msa_mode()` estimates `a1, a2` from it by maximum likelihood, returning a
point estimate plus an asymptotic covariance from the Hessian:


```r
fit <- fit_lrmsd_msa_mode(spm, observed$mode, observed$lrmsd_obs)
c(a1 = fit$a1, a2 = fit$a2)
#>         a1         a2 
#>  0.4492209 40.8195734
```



Table: ML estimate of the selection parameters (se from the Hessian)

|parameter | estimate|    se|
|:---------|--------:|-----:|
|a1        |    0.449| 0.058|
|a2        |   40.820| 6.314|



### Fitted vs. observed

An observed profile fixes the *shape* of the mode divergence but not its overall level,
so we compare shapes: each profile with its own mean subtracted off (`nlrmsd = lrmsd -
mean`). We build the fitted profile at the ML estimate — the `lrmsd_msa` column of the
fitted decomposition — join it to the observed one, and centre both.

We score the fit with `D²`, the deviance explained relative to a flat (mean-only) null:
`D² = 1 - deviance/null_deviance`. The fitter computed it over exactly the modes it
scored, so we read it off the fit object as `fit$gof$D2` rather than recomputing it.
Note it is `D²`, not `R²`: the model predicts divergence on a fixed scale, and `D²`
measures agreement with the prediction *as it stands*, where `R²` would credit a
prediction that is right only up to an arbitrary rescaling.


```r
predicted <- calculate_profiles(spm, fit$a1, fit$a2, metric = "lrmsd")$mode |>
  transmute(mode, lrmsd_fit = lrmsd_msa)

observed_vs_predicted <- observed |>
  inner_join(predicted, by = "mode") |>
  mutate(
    nlrmsd_obs = lrmsd_obs - mean(lrmsd_obs),
    nlrmsd_fit = lrmsd_fit - mean(lrmsd_fit)
  )

fit_d2 <- fit$gof$D2
```




```r
ggplot(observed_vs_predicted_long, aes(mode, nlrmsd, colour = source)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("observed" = "grey25", "fitted" = "firebrick")) +
  annotate("text", x = -Inf, y = Inf, hjust = -0.15, vjust = 1.8,
           label = sprintf("D^2 == %.3f", fit_d2), parse = TRUE) +
  labs(title = "Observed vs. fitted mode profile",
       x = "Normal-mode index", y = "nlrmsd (mean-centered)", colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

![plot of chunk mode-fit-profile](mode-analysis_files/figure-html/mode-fit-profile-1.png)


```r
ggplot(observed_vs_predicted, aes(nlrmsd_obs, nlrmsd_fit)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, colour = "grey70", linetype = 2) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4, colour = "steelblue") +
  annotate("text", x = -Inf, y = Inf, hjust = -0.15, vjust = 1.4,
           label = sprintf("D^2 == %.3f", fit_d2), parse = TRUE) +
  labs(title = "Fitted vs. observed mode divergence (mean-centered)",
       x = "observed nlrmsd", y = "fitted nlrmsd")
```

![plot of chunk mode-fit-scatter](mode-analysis_files/figure-html/mode-fit-scatter-1.png)

## 6. Decomposing the fitted profile

Section 3 decomposed the profile at a *chosen* `(a1, a2)`. The same
$\phi_{\text{mut}}/\phi_{\text{stab}}/\phi_{\text{act}}$ decomposition applies to
the **fitted** profile — call `calculate_decomposition()` at the ML estimate
`(fit$a1, fit$a2)` instead of the chosen strengths, and read the `phi_*` columns.
(The fit is to synthetic data, so this decomposes a synthetic-fitted profile.)


```r
decomposition_fit <- calculate_decomposition(spm, fit$a1, fit$a2, metric = "lrmsd")$mode
```

The mutation term is the divergence under no selection; a negative selection term
means that pressure *reduces* divergence at that mode relative to the
mutation-only model.


```r
decomposition_fit_long <- decomposition_fit |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(phi_mut, phi_stab, phi_act),
                      names_to = "component", values_to = "phi") |>
  mutate(component = factor(component, levels = names(component_colours)))
ggplot(decomposition_fit_long, aes(mode, phi, colour = component)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey80") +
  geom_line() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = component_colours, guide = "none") +
  facet_wrap(~ component, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(title = "Decomposition of the fitted profile",
       x = "Normal-mode index", y = "contribution to lrmsd")
```

![plot of chunk decomposition-fit](mode-analysis_files/figure-html/decomposition-fit-1.png)
